---
name: CI/CD

# The path a change takes:
#
#   pull request   ->  the app's checks, the hosting's checks, a diff against both environments
#                      (a fork's pull request gets the checks only)
#   merge queue    ->  the checks again, on main with the queued pull requests merged onto it; no diffs
#   merge to main  ->  build the app, deploy dev (the site stack publishes the build), seed the catalog, tag a release
#   release        ->  "Deploy Production" takes it from there
#
# Production is reached only through a published release, so it always carries
# a version and has always already been to dev. One repository, one pipeline:
# the app and its hosting change together and go out together.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump:
        description: Which part of the version to increment; auto reads the conventional commit titles since the last tag
        required: true
        default: auto
        type: choice
        options: [auto, patch, minor, major]
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  # The merge queue builds a branch with the queued pull requests merged onto
  # main and asks for the same checks on it, so a pull request that went green
  # on a stale base is tested and diffed again as it will actually land.
  merge_group:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

env:
  NODE_VERSION: 22
  # CloudFront will not accept a certificate issued anywhere else, and one
  # region avoids a cross-region reference for the sake of one certificate.
  AWS_REGION: us-east-1
  GITHUB_ROLE_NAME: GitHubActionRole

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  Test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [22]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Setup Node and run npm ci
        uses: ./.github/actions/npm-ci
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      # First of the checks, because it is the cheapest and it fails for
      # a reason none of the others can catch: a pack edited in place at
      # the version it already had reaches a library by id and version,
      # so nobody holding the old one is ever offered it. It used to run
      # after the suite, which meant waiting a minute and a half to be
      # told to change one line.
      #
      # Asked of the pull request, where there is a before to compare
      # against; the merge queue has already asked it of each one.
      - name: A changed pack says so in its version
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "$BASE"
          npm run check:pack-versions -- "$BASE"

      - run: npm run typecheck

      # Style for the docs, from .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc, so the prose
      # stays consistent without anybody holding the rules in their head.
      - run: npm run lint:docs

      # And style for the code, from .prettierrc.json. The pre-commit hook
      # does this on the way in, but a hook is a convenience: it arrives
      # with `npm install`, it is skipped by `npm ci --ignore-scripts`,
      # and `--no-verify` walks past it. This is the gate.
      - run: npm run format:check

      # The same shape the hosting's job has: the run writes JUnit beside
      # its console output, and the step below turns it into a check with
      # every test named, so a failure here reads the way a failure there
      # already did instead of sending somebody into the log.
      - run: npm run test:ci

      - name: Publish the app and engine test results
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v3
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: App and engine tests
          path: junit.xml
          reporter: java-junit
          fail-on-error: true

      # The packs that ship are held to the same standard a contributor's is:
      # --strict fails on warnings, and each pack's own fixtures are replayed
      # against the engine that plays them.
      - run: npm run check:packs
      - run: npm run test:packs

      - run: npm run build

  InfraTest:
    name: Test the hosting
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        aws-environment: [dev, prd]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Setup Node and run npm ci
        uses: ./.github/actions/npm-ci
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      # No credentials, and no real account: the stacks are asserted against
      # a synthesized template, so the tests need an account id to render
      # into ARNs and nothing more. A stand-in does that on a fork's pull
      # request as well as here, and keeps the real ids out of the picture.
      - name: Test the hosting against ${{ matrix.aws-environment }}
        env:
          AWS_REGION: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          AWS_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ matrix.aws-environment }}
          CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT: "123456789012"
          CDK_DEFAULT_REGION: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
        run: npm run test:ci -w hosted/infra

      - name: Publish the hosting's test results for ${{ matrix.aws-environment }}
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v3
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: Hosting tests (${{ matrix.aws-environment }})
          path: hosted/infra/junit.xml
          reporter: java-junit
          fail-on-error: true

  # The app is built before a diff or a deploy, so the site stack's template
  # names the build it would publish; a diff without one would show the
  # publish being torn down.
  #
  # Which is also why a diff is only read where the hosting changed. The
  # site stack names the build by its hash, so every pull request that
  # touches the app at all produces a diff, and a diff produced by every
  # pull request is one nobody reads. The job still runs and still
  # reports; where nothing under the hosting changed it says so and stops
  # there, rather than spending two AWS round-trips to print the same
  # asset hash again.
  Diff:
    name: Diff ${{ matrix.env }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      pull-requests: write
    # The diff itself runs on the pull request only, where a person reads
    # it. The merge queue runs the tests again on the combined branch but
    # not the diffs: a diff is for reading, and a change that no longer
    # synthesizes fails the deploy before any release is cut. The job still
    # runs in the queue with its steps skipped, so that each matrix entry
    # reports under its own name: a job skipped whole never expands its
    # matrix and reports as "Diff ${{ matrix.env }}", which the ruleset
    # does not recognize as "Diff dev", and the queue waits for a check
    # that never comes. Nothing that reaches AWS runs for a pull request
    # from a fork (GitHub would refuse it the OIDC token anyway), nor for
    # Dependabot's, which run without the repository's secrets and so
    # cannot name an account: a dependency bump is diffed in the queue's
    # deploy, not here.
    if: >-
      ${{
        github.event_name == 'merge_group'
        || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]')
      }}
    # Alongside the tests, not after them: a diff needs the built app and
    # nothing the tests decide, and waiting for them doubled the time a
    # pull request took to go green. The ruleset requires every check, so
    # a failing test still holds the merge.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        env: [dev, prd]
    # A stage's environment holds what the stage is: its account, its zone,
    # its sign-in client, under the same names in every stage, so this job
    # names nothing but the stage. It is open to this repository's
    # branches, since a diff is what a pull request asks for; the deploy
    # environments below are not.
    environment: cdk-diff-${{ matrix.env }}
    steps:
      - if: ${{ github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}
        run: echo "No diff in the merge queue; the pull request carried it. This job only reports."

      # What this pull request could change about a template: the stacks
      # themselves, the actions that build and synthesize them, and the
      # lockfile, which is where a CDK bump lands. Everything else is the
      # app, and the app's only mark on a template is the hash of the
      # build being published.
      - id: touches
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        name: Anything the hosting would notice
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          hosting=false
          while IFS= read -r f; do
            case "$f" in
              hosted/infra/* | package-lock.json | .github/workflows/CI-CD.yml | .github/actions/run-cdk/* | .github/actions/build-app/*)
                echo "the hosting changed: $f"
                hosting=true
                ;;
            esac
          done < <(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/files" --paginate -q '.[].filename')
          if [ "$hosting" = false ]; then
            echo "Nothing under hosted/infra changed, so there is no template change to read." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "Nothing under hosted/infra changed; no diff to read."
          fi
          echo "hosting=$hosting" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.touches.outputs.hosting == 'true' }}
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.touches.outputs.hosting == 'true' }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/build-app
        with:
          environment: ${{ matrix.env }}
          workos-client-id: ${{ vars.WORKOS_CLIENT_ID }}
          target-account-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          env-config: ${{ vars[format('RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_{0}', matrix.env)] }}
      - if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.touches.outputs.hosting == 'true' }}
        name: Diff the ${{ matrix.env }} stacks
        uses: ./.github/actions/run-cdk
        with:
          cdk-command: diff
          target-account-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          env-config: ${{ vars[format('RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_{0}', matrix.env)] }}
          target-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          github-role-name: ${{ env.GITHUB_ROLE_NAME }}
          aws-environment: ${{ matrix.env }}
          hosted-zone-id: ${{ secrets.RUNLOG_ZONE_ID }}
          app-dist: apps/web/dist

  # The one check the ruleset requires. It waits for every check above and
  # says whether they all passed, so the ruleset need not know their names:
  # a matrix can grow, a job can be renamed, a job can be skipped where that
  # is right, and none of it is a ruleset edit. A check that failed or was
  # cancelled fails this one; a test that did not run at all fails it too,
  # since a run with no tests proves nothing; a diff skipped in the merge
  # queue, on a fork's pull request, or on Dependabot's, is expected and
  # passes.
  Checks:
    name: Checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [Test, InfraTest, Diff]
    if: ${{ always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group') }}
    steps:
      - env:
          TEST: ${{ needs.Test.result }}
          INFRA: ${{ needs.InfraTest.result }}
          DIFF: ${{ needs.Diff.result }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          SAME_REPO: ${{ github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
          DEPENDABOT: ${{ github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "Test: $TEST; hosting tests: $INFRA; diffs: $DIFF ($EVENT)"
          ok=true
          [ "$TEST" = "success" ] || { echo "::error::the app's checks did not pass ($TEST)"; ok=false; }
          [ "$INFRA" = "success" ] || { echo "::error::the hosting's checks did not pass ($INFRA)"; ok=false; }
          case "$DIFF" in
            success) ;;
            skipped) if [ "$EVENT" = "merge_group" ] || [ "$SAME_REPO" != "true" ] || [ "$DEPENDABOT" = "true" ]; then echo "The diffs were skipped here, as expected."; else echo "::error::the diffs did not run"; ok=false; fi ;;
            *) echo "::error::the diffs did not pass ($DIFF)"; ok=false ;;
          esac
          $ok

  DevDeploy:
    name: Deploy Dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Restricted to main, so a deploy cannot be run from any other ref, and
    # holding the same secret names as the diff's environment.
    environment: deploy-dev
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    # One dev deploy at a time; a second merge waits behind the first. The
    # release is cut by the job after this one, in a lane of its own, so a
    # release waiting on a person never holds up the next dev deploy.
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-dev
      cancel-in-progress: false
    if: >-
      ${{
        (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
        || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      }}
    # The version this build was made with, for the release to tag and no other.
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      # Full history, or `git tag -l` sees nothing and every build is 0.0.1.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # The version this build becomes when it is released: the tag after
      # the latest, decided here so the footer on dev says the number the
      # release will carry, and the Release job below tags that number and
      # no other. Two builds waiting on a release may both name the same
      # next number; the release job refuses a number already taken, and
      # the newer build's release supersedes the older one's while it waits.
      #
      # How big the step is comes from the commits since the last tag; see
      # .github/scripts/next-version.sh, which the release job runs again
      # when the number was taken in the meantime. A manual run may say the
      # bump outright; its default, auto, reads the titles.
      - name: Work out the version this build becomes
        id: version
        run: bash .github/scripts/next-version.sh "${{ github.event.inputs.bump || 'auto' }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: ./.github/actions/build-app
        with:
          environment: dev
          workos-client-id: ${{ vars.WORKOS_CLIENT_ID }}
          target-account-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          env-config: ${{ vars.RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_DEV }}
          version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      - name: Deploy the hosting and publish the build to dev
        uses: ./.github/actions/run-cdk
        with:
          cdk-command: deploy
          target-account-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          env-config: ${{ vars.RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_DEV }}
          target-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          github-role-name: ${{ env.GITHUB_ROLE_NAME }}
          aws-environment: dev
          hosted-zone-id: ${{ secrets.RUNLOG_ZONE_ID }}
          app-dist: apps/web/dist

      # The stage, asked through its own edge: the API as JSON, the app's
      # script as JavaScript. A deploy that leaves either wrong fails here,
      # and a failed dev deploy cuts no release, so production never sees it.
      - name: Prove the stage answers
        uses: ./.github/actions/smoke
        with:
          env-config: ${{ vars.RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_DEV }}

      # The built-ins, listed in the catalog as the platform's own, so the
      # feed carries everything. Needs a key for the platform publisher's
      # account in the environment's RUNLOG_API_KEY; without one the step
      # says so and the bundle stays the catalog.
      - name: Seed the catalog with the built-in packs
        env:
          RUNLOG_API: https://runlog.dev.scrthq.com/api
          RUNLOG_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.RUNLOG_API_KEY }}
        run: npm run seed:listings

      - run: echo "### Deployed \`${GITHUB_SHA:0:12}\` to dev" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # The release: the tag, the notes and the GitHub release that production
  # and the package publish deploy from. Behind the `release` environment,
  # which requires a reviewer, so nothing reaches production or the registry
  # until a person has said so; the dev deploy above needs no such word.
  #
  # Its own lane, with in-progress runs kept: a release being cut finishes,
  # and while one waits for its reviewer the next merge's release takes its
  # place in the queue (GitHub keeps one pending run per lane, the newest),
  # so approving the newest releases everything merged so far, once. What
  # a superseded run would have tagged, the newer one tags; a number already
  # taken is refused rather than reused.
  Release:
    name: Tag and publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: DevDeploy
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: read
    concurrency:
      group: release
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      # Full history, for the tags and the notes since the last one.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # The number the dev build was made with, and no other: a footer on
      # dev that says 0.0.140 is followed by a release called v0.0.140.
      - name: Take the version this build was made with
        id: release
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          next="${{ needs.DevDeploy.outputs.tag }}"
          if [ -z "$next" ]; then echo "::error::the deploy named no version"; exit 1; fi
          # Two builds waiting on a release both name the same next number;
          # once the older one is approved and tagged, the newer counts
          # again from the tag it made, since its commits include the
          # older's. The footer on dev said the old number for a while; the
          # release says the true one, and the summary says it moved.
          if git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/${next}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "${next} is tagged already: a release cut while this one waited took it. Counting again from the latest tag."
            git fetch --tags --quiet origin
            eval "$(bash .github/scripts/next-version.sh auto)"
            echo "moved=${next} -> ${tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            next="$tag"
          fi
          echo "next=${next}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # A GitHub App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN. Anything GITHUB_TOKEN does is
      # barred from starting another run, and that applies to published
      # releases and pushed tags alike. A release created by the App fires
      # the `release: published` event, and production picks it up.
      - name: Mint a token that can trigger the release event
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.CODE_MGR_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.CODE_MGR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      # The notes are the commit titles since the last tag, grouped by type
      # as cliff.toml says; the whole changelog, every release back to the
      # first, goes on the release as a file rather than into the tree, since
      # nothing but this job may write to main.
      - name: Write the release notes
        id: notes
        uses: orhun/git-cliff-action@v4
        with:
          config: cliff.toml
          args: --unreleased --tag ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }} --strip all
        env:
          OUTPUT: RELEASE_NOTES.md
      - name: Write the whole changelog
        uses: orhun/git-cliff-action@v4
        with:
          config: cliff.toml
          args: --tag ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}
        env:
          OUTPUT: CHANGELOG.md

      - name: Tag and publish
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release create "${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}" \
            --target "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --title "${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}" \
            --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md \
            --latest \
            CHANGELOG.md

          {
            echo "### Released ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}"
            echo ""
            if [ -n "${{ steps.release.outputs.moved }}" ]; then echo "The number moved on the way: ${{ steps.release.outputs.moved }}, because a release approved in between took the one dev was built with."; echo ""; fi
            echo "Production deploys from the release event."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

---
name: CI/CD

# The path a change takes:
#
#   pull request   ->  the app's checks, the hosting's checks, a diff against both environments
#                      (a fork's pull request gets the checks only)
#   merge queue    ->  the checks again, on main with the queued pull requests merged onto it; no diffs
#   merge to main  ->  build the app, deploy dev (the site stack publishes the build), seed the catalog, tag a release
#   release        ->  "Deploy Production" takes it from there
#
# Production is reached only through a published release, so it always carries
# a version and has always already been to dev. One repository, one pipeline:
# the app and its hosting change together and go out together.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump:
        description: Which part of the version to increment; auto reads the conventional commit titles since the last tag
        required: true
        default: auto
        type: choice
        options: [auto, patch, minor, major]
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  # The merge queue builds a branch with the queued pull requests merged onto
  # main and asks for the same checks on it, so a pull request that went green
  # on a stale base is tested and diffed again as it will actually land.
  merge_group:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

env:
  NODE_VERSION: 22
  # CloudFront will not accept a certificate issued anywhere else, and one
  # region avoids a cross-region reference for the sake of one certificate.
  AWS_REGION: us-east-1
  GITHUB_ROLE_NAME: GitHubActionRole

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  Test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [22]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Setup Node and run npm ci
        uses: ./.github/actions/npm-ci
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      # First of the checks, because it is the cheapest and it fails for
      # a reason none of the others can catch: a pack edited in place at
      # the version it already had reaches a library by id and version,
      # so nobody holding the old one is ever offered it. It used to run
      # after the suite, which meant waiting a minute and a half to be
      # told to change one line.
      #
      # Asked of the pull request, where there is a before to compare
      # against; the merge queue has already asked it of each one.
      - name: A changed pack says so in its version
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "$BASE"
          npm run check:pack-versions -- "$BASE"

      - run: npm run typecheck

      # Style for the docs, from .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc, so the prose
      # stays consistent without anybody holding the rules in their head.
      - run: npm run lint:docs

      # And style for the code, from .prettierrc.json. The pre-commit hook
      # does this on the way in, but a hook is a convenience: it arrives
      # with `npm install`, it is skipped by `npm ci --ignore-scripts`,
      # and `--no-verify` walks past it. This is the gate.
      - run: npm run format:check

      # The same shape the hosting's job has: the run writes JUnit beside
      # its console output, and the step below turns it into a check with
      # every test named, so a failure here reads the way a failure there
      # already did instead of sending somebody into the log.
      - run: npm run test:ci

      - name: Publish the app and engine test results
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v3
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: App and engine tests
          path: junit.xml
          reporter: java-junit
          fail-on-error: true

      # The packs that ship are held to the same standard a contributor's is:
      # --strict fails on warnings, and each pack's own fixtures are replayed
      # against the engine that plays them.
      - run: npm run check:packs
      - run: npm run test:packs

      - run: npm run build

  InfraTest:
    name: Test the hosting
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        aws-environment: [dev, prd]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Setup Node and run npm ci
        uses: ./.github/actions/npm-ci
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      # No credentials, and no real account: the stacks are asserted against
      # a synthesized template, so the tests need an account id to render
      # into ARNs and nothing more. A stand-in does that on a fork's pull
      # request as well as here, and keeps the real ids out of the picture.
      - name: Test the hosting against ${{ matrix.aws-environment }}
        env:
          AWS_REGION: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          AWS_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ matrix.aws-environment }}
          CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT: "123456789012"
          CDK_DEFAULT_REGION: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
        run: npm run test:ci -w hosted/infra

      - name: Publish the hosting's test results for ${{ matrix.aws-environment }}
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v3
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: Hosting tests (${{ matrix.aws-environment }})
          path: hosted/infra/junit.xml
          reporter: java-junit
          fail-on-error: true

  # The app is built before a diff or a deploy, so the site stack's template
  # names the build it would publish; a diff without one would show the
  # publish being torn down.
  #
  # Which is also why a diff is only read where the hosting changed. The
  # site stack names the build by its hash, so every pull request that
  # touches the app at all produces a diff, and a diff produced by every
  # pull request is one nobody reads. The job still runs and still
  # reports; where nothing under the hosting changed it says so and stops
  # there, rather than spending two AWS round-trips to print the same
  # asset hash again.
  Diff:
    name: Diff ${{ matrix.env }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
      pull-requests: write
    # The diff itself runs on the pull request only, where a person reads
    # it. The merge queue runs the tests again on the combined branch but
    # not the diffs: a diff is for reading, and a change that no longer
    # synthesizes fails the deploy before any release is cut. The job still
    # runs in the queue with its steps skipped, so that each matrix entry
    # reports under its own name: a job skipped whole never expands its
    # matrix and reports as "Diff ${{ matrix.env }}", which the ruleset
    # does not recognize as "Diff dev", and the queue waits for a check
    # that never comes. Nothing that reaches AWS runs for a pull request
    # from a fork (GitHub would refuse it the OIDC token anyway), nor for
    # Dependabot's, which run without the repository's secrets and so
    # cannot name an account: a dependency bump is diffed in the queue's
    # deploy, not here.
    if: >-
      ${{
        github.event_name == 'merge_group'
        || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]')
      }}
    # Alongside the tests, not after them: a diff needs the built app and
    # nothing the tests decide, and waiting for them doubled the time a
    # pull request took to go green. The ruleset requires every check, so
    # a failing test still holds the merge.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        env: [dev, prd]
    # A stage's environment holds what the stage is: its account, its zone,
    # its sign-in client, under the same names in every stage, so this job
    # names nothing but the stage. It is open to this repository's
    # branches, since a diff is what a pull request asks for; the deploy
    # environments below are not.
    environment: cdk-diff-${{ matrix.env }}
    steps:
      - if: ${{ github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}
        run: echo "No diff in the merge queue; the pull request carried it. This job only reports."

      # What this pull request could change about a template: the stacks
      # themselves, the actions that build and synthesize them, and the
      # lockfile, which is where a CDK bump lands. Everything else is the
      # app, and the app's only mark on a template is the hash of the
      # build being published.
      - id: touches
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
        name: Anything the hosting would notice
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          hosting=false
          while IFS= read -r f; do
            case "$f" in
              hosted/infra/* | package-lock.json | .github/workflows/CI-CD.yml | .github/actions/run-cdk/* | .github/actions/build-app/*)
                echo "the hosting changed: $f"
                hosting=true
                ;;
            esac
          done < <(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/files" --paginate -q '.[].filename')
          if [ "$hosting" = false ]; then
            echo "Nothing under hosted/infra changed, so there is no template change to read." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "Nothing under hosted/infra changed; no diff to read."
          fi
          echo "hosting=$hosting" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.touches.outputs.hosting == 'true' }}
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.touches.outputs.hosting == 'true' }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/build-app
        with:
          environment: ${{ matrix.env }}
          workos-client-id: ${{ vars.WORKOS_CLIENT_ID }}
          target-account-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          env-config: ${{ vars[format('RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_{0}', matrix.env)] }}
      - if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && steps.touches.outputs.hosting == 'true' }}
        name: Diff the ${{ matrix.env }} stacks
        uses: ./.github/actions/run-cdk
        with:
          cdk-command: diff
          target-account-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          env-config: ${{ vars[format('RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_{0}', matrix.env)] }}
          target-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          github-role-name: ${{ env.GITHUB_ROLE_NAME }}
          aws-environment: ${{ matrix.env }}
          hosted-zone-id: ${{ secrets.RUNLOG_ZONE_ID }}
          app-dist: apps/web/dist

  # The one check the ruleset requires. It waits for every check above and
  # says whether they all passed, so the ruleset need not know their names:
  # a matrix can grow, a job can be renamed, a job can be skipped where that
  # is right, and none of it is a ruleset edit. A check that failed or was
  # cancelled fails this one; a test that did not run at all fails it too,
  # since a run with no tests proves nothing; a diff skipped in the merge
  # queue, on a fork's pull request, or on Dependabot's, is expected and
  # passes.
  Checks:
    name: Checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [Test, InfraTest, Diff]
    if: ${{ always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group') }}
    steps:
      - env:
          TEST: ${{ needs.Test.result }}
          INFRA: ${{ needs.InfraTest.result }}
          DIFF: ${{ needs.Diff.result }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          SAME_REPO: ${{ github.event_name == 'merge_group' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
          DEPENDABOT: ${{ github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "Test: $TEST; hosting tests: $INFRA; diffs: $DIFF ($EVENT)"
          ok=true
          [ "$TEST" = "success" ] || { echo "::error::the app's checks did not pass ($TEST)"; ok=false; }
          [ "$INFRA" = "success" ] || { echo "::error::the hosting's checks did not pass ($INFRA)"; ok=false; }
          case "$DIFF" in
            success) ;;
            skipped) if [ "$EVENT" = "merge_group" ] || [ "$SAME_REPO" != "true" ] || [ "$DEPENDABOT" = "true" ]; then echo "The diffs were skipped here, as expected."; else echo "::error::the diffs did not run"; ok=false; fi ;;
            *) echo "::error::the diffs did not pass ($DIFF)"; ok=false ;;
          esac
          $ok

  DevDeploy:
    name: Deploy Dev
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Restricted to main, so a deploy cannot be run from any other ref, and
    # holding the same secret names as the diff's environment.
    environment: deploy-dev
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    # One dev deploy at a time; a second merge waits behind the first. The
    # release is cut by the job after this one, in a lane of its own, so a
    # release waiting on a person never holds up the next dev deploy.
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-dev
      cancel-in-progress: false
    if: >-
      ${{
        (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
        || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      }}
    # The version this build was made with, for the release to tag and no other.
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      # Full history, or `git tag -l` sees nothing and every build is 0.0.1.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # The version this build becomes when it is released: the tag after
      # the latest, decided here so the footer on dev says the number the
      # release will carry, and the Release job below tags that number and
      # no other. Two builds waiting on a release may both name the same
      # next number; the release job refuses a number already taken, and
      # the newer build's release supersedes the older one's while it waits.
      #
      # How big the step is comes from the commits since the last tag; see
      # .github/scripts/next-version.sh, which the release job runs again
      # when the number was taken in the meantime. A manual run may say the
      # bump outright; its default, auto, reads the titles.
      - name: Work out the version this build becomes
        id: version
        run: bash .github/scripts/next-version.sh "${{ github.event.inputs.bump || 'auto' }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: ./.github/actions/build-app
        with:
          environment: dev
          workos-client-id: ${{ vars.WORKOS_CLIENT_ID }}
          target-account-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          env-config: ${{ vars.RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_DEV }}
          version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      - name: Deploy the hosting and publish the build to dev
        uses: ./.github/actions/run-cdk
        with:
          cdk-command: deploy
          target-account-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          env-config: ${{ vars.RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_DEV }}
          target-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          github-role-name: ${{ env.GITHUB_ROLE_NAME }}
          aws-environment: dev
          hosted-zone-id: ${{ secrets.RUNLOG_ZONE_ID }}
          app-dist: apps/web/dist

      # The stage, asked through its own edge: the API as JSON, the app's
      # script as JavaScript. A deploy that leaves either wrong fails here,
      # and a failed dev deploy cuts no release, so production never sees it.
      - name: Prove the stage answers
        uses: ./.github/actions/smoke
        with:
          env-config: ${{ vars.RUNLOG_ENV_CONFIG_DEV }}

      # The built-ins, listed in the catalog as the platform's own, so the
      # feed carries everything. Needs a key for the platform publisher's
      # account in the environment's RUNLOG_API_KEY; without one the step
      # says so and the bundle stays the catalog.
      - name: Seed the catalog with the built-in packs
        env:
          RUNLOG_API: https://runlog.dev.scrthq.com/api
          RUNLOG_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.RUNLOG_API_KEY }}
        run: npm run seed:listings

      - run: echo "### Deployed \`${GITHUB_SHA:0:12}\` to dev" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # The release: the tag, the notes and the GitHub release that production
  # and the package publish deploy from. Behind the `release` environment,
  # which requires a reviewer, so nothing reaches production or the registry
  # until a person has said so; the dev deploy above needs no such word.
  #
  # Its own lane, with in-progress runs kept: a release being cut finishes,
  # and while one waits for its reviewer the next merge's release takes its
  # place in the queue (GitHub keeps one pending run per lane, the newest),
  # so approving the newest releases everything merged so far, once. What
  # a superseded run would have tagged, the newer one tags; a number already
  # taken is refused rather than reused.
  Release:
    name: Tag and publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: DevDeploy
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: read
    concurrency:
      group: release
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      # Full history, for the tags and the notes since the last one.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # The number the dev build was made with, and no other: a footer on
      # dev that says 0.0.140 is followed by a release called v0.0.140.
      - name: Take the version this build was made with
        id: release
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          next="${{ needs.DevDeploy.outputs.tag }}"
          if [ -z "$next" ]; then echo "::error::the deploy named no version"; exit 1; fi
          # Two builds waiting on a release both name the same next number;
          # once the older one is approved and tagged, the newer counts
          # again from the tag it made, since its commits include the
          # older's. The footer on dev said the old number for a while; the
          # release says the true one, and the summary says it moved.
          if git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/${next}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "${next} is tagged already: a release cut while this one waited took it. Counting again from the latest tag."
            git fetch --tags --quiet origin
            eval "$(bash .github/scripts/next-version.sh auto)"
            echo "moved=${next} -> ${tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            next="$tag"
          fi
          echo "next=${next}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # A GitHub App token, not GITHUB_TOKEN. Anything GITHUB_TOKEN does is
      # barred from starting another run, and that applies to published
      # releases and pushed tags alike. A release created by the App fires
      # the `release: published` event, and production picks it up.
      - name: Mint a token that can trigger the release event
        id: app-token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.CODE_MGR_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.CODE_MGR_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      # The notes are the commit titles since the last tag, grouped by type
      # as cliff.toml says; the whole changelog, every release back to the
      # first, goes on the release as a file rather than into the tree, since
      # nothing but this job may write to main.
      - name: Write the release notes
        id: notes
        uses: orhun/git-cliff-action@v4
        with:
          config: cliff.toml
          args: --unreleased --tag ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }} --strip all
        env:
          OUTPUT: RELEASE_NOTES.md
      - name: Write the whole changelog
        uses: orhun/git-cliff-action@v4
        with:
          config: cliff.toml
          args: --tag ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}
        env:
          OUTPUT: CHANGELOG.md

      - name: Tag and publish
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release create "${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}" \
            --target "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --title "${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}" \
            --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md \
            --latest \
            CHANGELOG.md

          {
            echo "### Released ${{ steps.release.outputs.next }}"
            echo ""
            if [ -n "${{ steps.release.outputs.moved }}" ]; then echo "The number moved on the way: ${{ steps.release.outputs.moved }}, because a release approved in between took the one dev was built with."; echo ""; fi
            echo "Production deploys from the release event."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

inputs:
  node-version:
    description: "Node version to use"
    required: false
    default: 22

runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
      with:
        node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}

    - name: Cache node modules
      id: cache-npm
      uses: actions/cache@v6
      env:
        cache-name: cache-node-modules
      with:
        path: ~/.npm
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-build-${{ env.cache-name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-build-${{ env.cache-name }}-
          ${{ runner.os }}-build-
          ${{ runner.os }}-

    - run: npm ci --cache ~/.npm --prefer-offline
      shell: bash

# script that does not read this file.
**/dist/
**/cdk.out/
**/stage/
**/node_modules/
packages/rules-schema/schema/
apps/web/dist/
docs/reference.md
junit.xml
package-lock.json

# The packs are documents, not code.
#
# A pack is written to be read as a rulebook: tables are one line per
# entry so a d100 reads like the paper it came from, and a folded block
# is wrapped where the sentence wants to break. Prettier would explode
# every flow-style entry into eight lines of block YAML and reflow prose
# it cannot tell from data. There is already a linter, a schema and a
# validator holding these to a standard; none of them care about column
# width, and neither should this.
packs/

# Someone else's four hundred place names and nine hundred item names,
# generated from a tool's own resources. See tests/license-boundary.test.ts.
apps/web/src/control/lists/

# The Remember plugin scratch area, not part of the project.
.remember/

# Entire's scratch, logs and transcripts. Its own .gitignore holds these
# back from git; prettier does not read nested ignore files, so they are
# named again here. The two tracked files beside them are formatted.
.entire/tmp/
.entire/logs/
.entire/metadata/

# Markdown belongs to markdownlint-cli2, which already has a considered
# config for it (.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc) and a reason for the rule that
# matters: one line per paragraph, no fill column, so a one-word edit
# does not touch the whole paragraph. Prettier would also rewrite
# emphasis style and pad every table column, which is churn nobody asked
# for.
*.md

# Deployed page templates, filled in by hosted/scripts/overlay.ts.
#
# `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` is not valid JSON and these are not source: they are
# hand-written pages with a substitution step, and the legal ones say
# only what counsel has confirmed. Reformatting them buys nothing and
# puts a diff through text that is checked by a person, not a parser.
hosted/pages/
